description: Whether an ordinary http/https page sees chrome.runtime and window.browser, which is decided entirely by whether some installed extension's externally_connectable manifest key matches the page: CanWebpageContextConnectExternally in extensions/renderer/native_extension_bindings_system.cc walks the renderer's extension set and returns true on the first match, and UpdateBindingsForContext installs the runtime accessor and the browser object from that answer alone. Conditioned on nothing. It is a fact about what the machine's owner installed, and nothing else in a profile predicts that: the same wallet extension is on Windows, macOS and Linux desktops alike, so keying this on the platform or the machine class would invent a correlation the population does not have. Presence-only by design -- the axis never names an extension id, because a fixed id is a cross-instance correlator that survives every other axis, and an inert component extension shipped to supply one would be worse than the surface it closes.
label: extensions

options.note: MEASURED, and the state of every profile: a browser with no extension matching the page has no chrome.runtime there, so false is what fresh Chrome reports. It is served as an explicit false rather than as an absent section, which leaves only the extensions really installed in the profile to decide, as in stock Chrome: a Google-owned extension on its own origins, or an extension the user installed that names the page. A drawn externally-connectable state showed chrome.runtime on every page for a quarter of seeds, which no install does without such an extension, so it is no longer drawn.
options.source: own measurement, stock Google Chrome 153.0.8010.48 on a fresh --user-data-dir: Object.getOwnPropertyNames(chrome) is ['loadTimes','csi','app'] and typeof chrome.runtime is 'undefined' on https://example.com/ and on file:///; Apostate 152 matches it field for field under a composed Windows persona
